title: Cost Center × Appointment-Centric
summary: Service protects the product sale and is managed to cost. Work is booked visits to a location, and the customer judges success by whether the technician arrived in the window.
contrastLine: Same method, different cell: the blueprint shifts from margin and entitlement to schedule reliability and cost per visit.
focusJobs: Offer and confirm appointment windows the customer can self-book
Optimize routes to minimize travel cost per visit
Capture completion and customer sign-off on mobile

kpis.name: On-time arrival rate
kpis.definition: Share of visits where the technician arrived inside the booked window.
kpis.whyItMatters: In an appointment-centric cell the window is the promise. Missing it is the failure the customer remembers.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Rising, with late arrivals traced to scheduling, travel, or overrunning prior jobs.

kpis.name: Cost per visit
kpis.definition: Total field labor, travel, and overhead divided by completed visits.
kpis.whyItMatters: When service is a cost center, the operating goal is delivering the same promise for less.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Falling without on-time arrival or satisfaction falling with it.

kpis.name: Completed visits per technician day
kpis.definition: Average number of visits a technician completes in a working day.
kpis.whyItMatters: Route density and schedule quality show up here before they show up in cost.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Rising through better routing, not through shorter, rushed visits.

kpis.name: Customer satisfaction after visit
kpis.definition: Post-visit survey score on the appointment experience.
kpis.whyItMatters: Service exists to protect the relationship and the next product sale.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Stable or rising as cost per visit falls.
